This is a list of the best-selling video gamefranchises worldwide, ranked up to 50th place by reported software unit sales. _Mario "Mario (franchise)")_ is the best-selling video game franchise of all time, with over 893 million units sold since its first commercial release in 1983. Nintendo, the publisher of _Mario_, has the most franchises on the list with eight entries.For this list, sales figures must be directly attributed to a franchise to be included. In instances where overall figures for a franchise are not known but sales of a single game within that franchise are, sales for that game will be attributed to the franchise. Sales of expansion packs and episodic video games are included. Metrics such as "players" or "installs" are not listed as they typically refer to user engagement rather than sales; even for paid games, these metrics could include free trials or other free promotions and cannot reliably be substituted for sales figures.

The listed publisher correspond to each franchise's most recent release, and release years refer only to the first commercial launch, excluding any pre-release stages. Rankings serve solely for numbering purposes and are not meant to be precise, reflecting the list's limited scope because there is no credible, comprehensive sales-tracking source for the video game industry,( unlike for films, which have box office tracking sites such as _Box Office Mojo_ and _The Numbers "The Numbers (website)")_. # Best-Selling Video Game Franchises of All Time (1994 - 2026)
## Favoree

Posted: 21 Nov 2025
👋 Welcome to the Ultimate Chart Race of the top 10 biggest game franchises in history (number of copies sold).

🏆 List of the top box-office franchises in November 2025:

- Call Of Duty
- Pokémon
- GTA
- Mario Bros
- Minecraft

Source: Bloomberg, Forbes, Wikipedia, Company Reports

YouTube: @favoree-io  
Website:

LinkedIn: 

DISCLAIMER: This comparison is based on public data, surveys, public comments & discussions and approximate estimations that might be subjected to some degree of error
 

#bestsellinggame #topgames #gta #gta6 #callofduty  #pokemon  #boxoffice31 comments
### Transcript:I love video games and the one thing they do the best is franchises. Every new Final Fantasy is a spectacle. Every new Zelda game is a real adventure and every new Pokémon is just a little bit more disappointing than the last one. But which game franchise sells best? Let's find out. Starting off with the Mario Brothers, a franchise that catapulted video games into the mainstream. The first appearance of everyone's favorite plumber was in Donkey Kong, a true arcade classic that is still played to this day. Donkey Kong was the first big success for Nintendo when it came to video games. They had already been experimenting with electronic entertainment before that, but none of them hit like Donkey Kong. After that, Nintendo realized the true potential of investing in video games. first with the Mario Brothers arcade game and then by developing their own console, the NES. And with that console came Super Mario Bros., one of the most successful video games in history. The famous plumbers became Nintendo's best cash cow, which is why they started putting them into everything they produced. Mario himself was in their tennis game, in their golf game, in their pinball game, even on some of the Game and Watches. Nintendo really put that character into everything and then later on created whole new spin-off franchises. There are so many, in fact, we ended up separating them from the mainline games on this chart race. Every single mainline Mario game was an absolute banger. Super Mario Bros. 1, 2, 3, and 4 were all in the bestselling video games of that time. The first Super Mario Bros. alone sold over 15 million copies by 1994. Nintendo just released banger after banger, and they would continue doing so to this day. We'll talk about them again later in this video. Until then, let's discuss Tetris, the runner-up on this list. Nintendo introduces Tetris. Put a piece here. Put a piece there. Tetris is one of those rare games that don't need flashy graphics or interesting story lines to sell millions. Created back in 1985 by a Soviet software engineer named Alex Bajit not. It slowly spread from office computers in Moscow to pretty much every platform you could imagine. But its real explosion came in 1989 when it released on the original Game Boy and NES. The Game Boy actually released bundled with the game in Europe and North America. That move alone turned Tetris into a global sensation, selling tens of millions of copies and helping make the Game Boy one of the most successful handhelds ever. By the mid to late '9s, it was hard to meet anyone who had never heard of Tetris before. The game had official releases on nearly every console available, from the NES to the SNES, the PlayStation, and the Nintendo 64. Even the arcade and PC versions kept selling with new variants appearing every couple of years. In 1996, Pajit finally regained the rights to his creation and together with Hank Rogers founded the Tetris company to manage and license it properly. This is when the franchise really solidified its identity, ensuring every version from then on would stay true to its original gameplay. By the late 90s, you had games like Tetrisphere and New Tetris, bringing fresh mechanics and 3D effects to the formula. But none of these changes and new gimmicks ever truly had the staying power of the original gameplay. New versions of the original game keep popping up to this day. And the NES version even has a competitive scene playing at a very high level. It's truly fascinating what Tetris was able to achieve. a puzzle game from the Soviet Union that managed to outlast trends, consoles, and even entire generations of players. And somehow it's still going strong today. Platformers like Mario and Sonic and puzzle games like Tetris are great, but the one kind of game that was dominating in the late '9s and early 2000s was the JRPGs. franchises like Dragon Quest, Final Fantasy, and most importantly, the one we're going to talk about next, Pokémon. [Music] The first few Pokémon games, also referred to as Gen 1, were released in 1996 in Japan. And then later on in 1998, Blue and Yellow also released internationally. Saying that Pokémon was a hit is an understatement. Together, the first generation sold over 25 million copies by the year 2000. Then in 1999, Pokemon Gold and Silver the second generation launched on the Game Boy Color, adding a new region, 100 new creatures and features like real-time clocks and color graphics. These two games, along with their enhanced version, Pokemon Crystal, sold roughly [...] the whole franchise above a majority of every other gaming franchise ever made. Before we get to the end of this, let's take a quick look at Mario Kart, a franchise that has remained on this list ever since it first appeared. Even though it's a spin-off of Super Mario Bros., [Music] Mario Kart is one of those franchises that is impossible to hate. They don't release a new game every single year. Their games are always enjoyable and easy to pick up. They have both a strong casual and competitive scene with speedrunning, and they're simply a blast to play in couch co-op with your friends. Every new Nintendo console has one of these, the exception being the Switch, as they just remastered the previous game for it. But turns out that this was a genius move because Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is the bestselling game in the franchise, selling over 70 million copies by itself, with Mario Kart Wii being the second best selling over 37 million copies. Mario Kart is by far the most popular spin-off franchise for Mario, but they have so many more than just that. For example, you have all the Mario Sports games. You have Mario Party, Super Smash Brothers, arguably, and even games like Super Mario Maker, which don't really fit any specific franchise. Together, every single Super Mario franchise has a combined sales number of close to a billion units. just a truly crazy number. If combined, no other franchise will even get close to Mario anytime soon. But the second place spot is still up for grabs. Currently, Call of Duty holds that position with over 500 million sales, but both Pokémon and GTA are not very far from it. Personally, I believe that the release of GTA 6 will be a turning point on this list, as GTA will be taking the top spot for a very long time. But who knows, maybe a new Mario game or a new Pokemon will completely change things up again. Let me know what you guys think in the comments. Have a good day and see you next

# The 10 Best-Selling Video Games of All Time

## 2024 update: GTA 5, Red Dead 2 keep climbing.

By Jordan Sirani

Updated:

327 comments

Games have always existed in a numbers-obsessed industry. Sega vs. Nintendo defined a generation in the '90s, while today's comparatively mild console wars and monthly reports keep sales figures near the forefront of games-related discussion. New monetization models require new metrics for success –monthly active users, player retention rates, in-game revenue, etc. Still, one of the industry's biggest questions remains: What are the best-selling video games of all time?

To answer this question, we've compiled the most accurate list possible by contacting publishers and digging through financial reports, news stories, interviews, and more. The result is the following list of the 10 best-selling video games of all time.

Some notes up front:

 Pack-in games are counted toward sales totals, considering most games on this list were, at one point, bundled with a console.
 Free downloads are not counted as sales, which excludes massively successful games like Fortnite and League of Legends from a list like this.
 Due to a lack of available sales data, we could not include certain games that may belong on this list. For example, we reached out to Activision seeking updated sales numbers for the Call of Duty franchise, but did not receive updated information to include those games on this list.

## 10. The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – 50 million+ [...] ## 3. Grand Theft Auto 5 – 200 million+

Grand Theft Auto 5 is the best-selling console/PC-only game of all time (the top two entries on this list have mobile versions). Sales of Rockstar’s ambitious open-world adventure passed 200 million units by the end of July 2024. That number compiles the game’s sales totals across three console generations and PC.

GTA 5 was the fastest entertainment release from any medium to reach $1 billion in retail sales — and it’s since earned Rockstar and Take-Two billions more, making it the most profitable entertainment release ever, at least as of 2018. Total sales for the franchise sit at 430 million units sold.

GTA 6 is now in development and due out in Fall 2025.

## 2. Minecraft – 300 million

has sold over 300 million copies as of October 2023, Mojang announced during this year's Minecraft Live (via Minecraft). That figure captures the sales total across Minecraft's many platforms. With film, Netflix, education, toy, and many other projects completed or in the works, Minecraft has transcended the medium in a way few others have before it.

## 1. Tetris – 520 million

Arguably the most timeless video game ever created, Tetris sits comfortably atop the list of all-time bestsellers with 520 million copies sold, according to The Tetris Company. That number includes sales across all available platforms, with the majority coming from mobile (425 million paid mobile downloads as of 2014, according to Henk Rogers, The Tetris Company's managing director).Tetris was initially released for the Soviet Union-developed Elektronika 60 computer, and variations of the classic puzzler have since been made for over 50 different platforms. Notably, it helped launch the Game Boy to success, eventually selling 35 million copies on Nintendo's handheld console.

Modern variations of the classic are still being released: Tetris Effect: Connected brought the puzzler to current-gen consoles with an emotional twist, and in 2020, SEGA released Puyo Puyo Tetris 2.

And those are the 10 best-selling video games at all time. Falling just outside these top-sellers are Pokemon's Generation 1 games (47 million), Super Mario Bros. (48 million) and Overwatch (50 million). Will any of the games on this be overtaken by Grand Theft Auto 6 or The Elder Scrolls 6 in the future? Only time will tell...
